How to read a listing

Eligible now date has passed; service can be cut on notice
Within 6 mo6–12 mo
  • POTS service discontinuance: the carrier has FCC permission (or has asked for it) to end traditional landline service. Dates are "on or after."
  • Copper retirement: the carrier is removing the copper network. Services that ride on copper, including alarm, elevator and fax lines, must move.
  • Match: "Exact" means the ZIP appears in the carrier's address list. "Community" means the wire center serves this town or city; wire center boundaries do not follow ZIP lines, so not every address is affected.

What this covers

Filings from AT&T, Verizon and Frontier (a Verizon company since Jan 20, 2026), Lumen/CenturyLink, Windstream, Consolidated, altafiber and Hawaiian Telcom with target dates from April 2026 through October 2027.

Sources are FCC Section 214 public notices, carrier copper-retirement notices under 47 CFR 51.333, and copies of carrier filings at state utility commissions. Each listing links to its source.

Some filings name only states, not wire centers. Those appear as state notices in the copper-colored boxes.

Before you rely on it

Carriers add filings every week, and approved dates can still move. A listing means a filing exists, not that a specific line will be cut on that date. Check the bill or the carrier's 90-day notice for the address, and plan the replacement for fire alarm, elevator, emergency phone and fax lines early: installers book up when a wire center closes.
